newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech blue chips push PSE higher, dealers positive.
newsitem.headline: Czech blue chips push PSE higher, dealers positive.

text.p: Strong gains to several Czech blue chips pushed the Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) higher on Wednesday, as renewed buying interest from abroad sparked dealer optimism of a modest upturn for the embattled bourse.
SPT Telecom, the PSE's most-capitalised issue, jumped 158 crowns to 3,132 while Komercni Banka shares edged up 35 crowns to 1,990 as the PX50 index firmed 5.0 points, or 1.01 percent, to 497.7.
Total volume was moderate with 737,741 shares changing hands on turnover of 594.6 million crowns. Overall, 122 shares gained ground, while 104 fell and 49 held steady.

The PSE, which has long-suffered from a lack of confidence among foreign investors who consider the market opaque, has been hit doubly hard in recent weeks by fears over a devaluation of the already-weakened crown.

But dealers said investors, especially from the U.S. and continental Europe were buying in "decent" volumes, after the recent market downturn and weakening of the crown made prices too attractive to pass up.

"The political uncertainty is a little less than last week, as has the negativeness over the crown...so I think this slight uptrend in somewhat sustainable," said Brian Jones of atlantik Financni Trhy.
"This is not the beginning of a major bull run, but it is a period of strengthening because people see shares here as essentially cheap," he added.
On the broader market, exhibition organiser BVV continued its strong run, rising 75 crowns at the fixing after recording a 120 jump on Tuesday.
